edition.locus: Adversus Marcionem 4.43 (sepulcrum / tertia die / corpus uerum)

source_text: Oportuerat etiam sepultorem domini prophetari ac iam tunc merito benedici, si nec mulierum illarum officium praeterit prophetia, quae ante lucem conuenerunt ad sepulcrum cum odorum paratura. de hoc enim per Osee: et quaerent, inquit, faciem meam; ante lucem uigilabunt ad me dicentes: eamus et conuertamur ad dominum, quia ipse eripuit [dixit] et curabit nos, percussit et miserebitur nostri, sanabit nos post biduum, in die tertia resurgemus. quis enim haec non credat in recogitatu mulierum illarum uolutata inter dolorem praesentis destitutionis, qua percussae sibi uidebantur a domino, et spem resurrectionis ipsius, qua restitutuiri se arbitrabantur? corpore autem non inuento sublata erat sepultura eius de medio secundum Esaiam. sed et duo ibidem angeli apparuerunt. tot fere laterensibus uti solebat in duobus testibus consistens dei sermo. reuertentes quoque a sepulcro mulieres et ab illa angelorum uisione prospiciebatEsaias: mulieres, inquit, [uenite] uenientes a uisione, uenite, ad renuntiandam scilicet domini resurrectionem. Bene autem,I quod incredulitas discipulorum perseuerabat, ut in finem usque defensio nostra consisteret Christum legum non alium se discipulis edidisse quam prophetarum. nam cum duo ex illis iter agerent et dominus eis adhaesisset, non comparens quod ipse esset, etiam dissimulans de conscientia rei gestae: nos autem putabamus, inquiunt, ipsum esse redemptorem Israhelis, utique suum Christum, id est creatoris. adeo nec alium se ediderat illis. ceterum non existimarent eum creatoris,I et cum creatoris existimaretur, non sustinuisset hanc de se existimationem, si non is esset, qui existimabatur. aut ipse! erit auctor erroris et praeuaricator ueritatis aduersus dei optimi titulum. sed nec post resurrectionem alium se eis ostendit quam quem existimatum sibi dixerant. plane inuectus est in illos: o insensati et tardi corde in non credendo omnibus, quae locutus est ad uos. quaenam locutus? alterius se dei esse? proba, et manus dedo. an eadem et angeli ad mulieres: rememoramini, quae locutus sit uobis in Galilaea dicens, quod oportet tradi filium hominis et crucifigi et tertia die resurgere? et quare oportebat, nisi quia ita a deo creatore scriptum? igitur increpuit illos ut de sola passione scandalizatos et ut dubios de fide resurrectionis adnuntiatae sibi a feminis, per quae non crediderant ipsum fuisse, quem existimauerant. itaque quod existimauerant, id uolens credi se eum se confirmabat, quem existimauerant, creatoris scilicet Christum, redemptorem Israhelis. De corporis autem ueritate quid potest clarius? cum haesitantibus eis, ne phantasma esset, immo phantasma credentibus: quid turbati estis? (in quit,) et quid cogitationes subeunt in corda uestra? uidete manus meas et pedes, quia ipse ego sum, quoniam spiritus ossa non habet, sicut me habentem uidetis. et Marcion quaedam contraria sibi illa, credo, industria eradere de euangelio suo noluit, ut ex his, quae eradere potuit nec erasit, illa, quae erasit, aut negetur erasisse aut merito erasisse dicatur; nec parcit nisi eis, quae non minus aliter interpretando quam delendo subuertit. uult itaque sic dictum: spiritus ossa non habet, sicut me uidetis habentem, quasi ad spiritum referatur sicut me uidetis habentem, id est non habentem ossa, sicut et spiritus. et quae ratio tortuositatis istius, cum simpliciter pronuntiare potuisset:. quia spiritus ossa non habet, sicut me uidetis non habentem? cur autem inspectui eorum manus et pedes suos offert, quae membra ex ossibus constant, si ossa non habebat? cur adicit: et scitote, quia ego sum, quem scilicet corporeum retro nouerant? aut si phantasma erat usquequaque, cur illos phantasma credentes increpabat? atquin adhuc eis non credentibus propterea cibum desiderauit, ut se ostenderet etiam dentes habere. Impleuimus, ut opinor, sponsionem. exhibuimus legum Christum prophetarum doctrinis sententiis adfectibus sensibus uirtutibus passionibus etiam resun-ectione non alium quam creatoris, siquidem et apostolos mittens ad praedicandum uniuersis nationibus in omnem terram exire sonum eorum et in terminos terrae uoces eorum psalmum adimplendo praecepit. misereor tui, Marcion; frustra laborasti. Christus enim Iesus in euangelio tuo meus est.
pass_a_gloss: Women at the tomb fulfill Hosea’s third-day rising; risen Lord confirms he is Creator’s redeemer of Israel; hands and feet with bones refute phantasm — Christ in Marcion’s gospel is still the Creator’s.
pass_b_english: The Lord’s burier also ought to have been prophesied and already then worthily blessed, if prophecy does not pass by those women’s office who before light gathered at the tomb with a preparation of spices. For of this through Hosea: And they will seek, he says, my face; before light they will watch for me saying: Let us go and turn to the Lord, because he himself has seized and will heal us, he struck and will pity us, he will heal us after two days, on the third day we will rise. For who would not believe these things rolled in those women’s thought between the pain of present forsaking, by which they seemed to themselves struck by the Lord, and the hope of his resurrection, by which they thought they would be restored? And with the body not found, his burial had been taken up from the midst according to Isaiah. But also two angels appeared there — about as many side-helpers as God’s word was used to stand on in two witnesses. Isaiah also foresaw the women returning from the tomb and from that angels’ vision: Women, he says, coming from the vision, come — to announce of course the Lord’s resurrection. And it is well that the disciples’ unbelief persisted, so that to the end our defense would stand: that Christ had shown himself to the disciples as no other than the prophets’. For when two of them were on the way and the Lord had joined them, not appearing as himself, even hiding knowledge of what was done: But we thought, they say, he was Israel’s redeemer — of course their Christ, that is the Creator’s. So he had not shown himself as another to them. Otherwise they would not have thought him the Creator’s; and when he was thought the Creator’s, he would not have borne this thought about himself if he were not the one thought. Else he himself will be author of error and traitor of truth against the best God’s title. But not even after the resurrection did he show himself to them as other than whom they had said they thought. Clearly he attacked them: O senseless and slow of heart in not believing all that he spoke to you. What things spoken? That he was of another god? Prove it, and I yield. Or the same things the angels also to the women: Remember what he spoke to you in Galilee, saying that the Son of man must be handed over and crucified and rise on the third day? And why must it, unless because so it was written by God the Creator? Therefore he rebuked them as scandalized only at the passion and as doubtful of the faith of the resurrection announced to them by the women — by which they had not believed he was the very one they had thought. So what they had thought, that he wanted believed: he confirmed himself as the one they had thought — of course the Creator’s Christ, Israel’s redeemer. But what can be clearer about the truth of the body? When they hesitated lest he be a phantasm — indeed believing a phantasm: Why are you troubled? he says, and why do thoughts enter your hearts? See my hands and my feet, because I myself am, since a spirit does not have bones as you see me having. And Marcion, I believe by industry, was unwilling to erase from his gospel certain things contrary to himself, so that from those he could erase and did not erase, those he did erase may either be denied erased or said rightly erased; nor does he spare except those he overturns no less by interpreting otherwise than by deleting. So he wants it said thus: A spirit does not have bones as you see me having — as if as you see me having were referred to the spirit, that is not having bones, as the spirit also. And what reason for this twist, when he could have pronounced simply: because a spirit does not have bones as you see me not having? But why does he offer their inspection his hands and feet, which members consist of bones, if he had no bones? Why add: And know that I am — whom of course they had known before as bodily? Or if he was a phantasm through and through, why rebuke them for believing a phantasm? Yet while they still did not believe he desired food for this reason: to show he even had teeth. We have fulfilled, I think, the pledge. We have exhibited the law’s Christ by the prophets’ teachings, sentences, affections, senses, powers, passions, even resurrection as no other than the Creator’s — since also sending apostles to preach to all nations he commanded, fulfilling the psalm, that their sound go out into all the earth and their voices to the ends of the earth. I pity you, Marcion; you have labored in vain. For Christ Jesus in your gospel is mine.
